title: Enforce cross-region tier contracts + safe fallback-model validator
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Replace multiple ad-hoc runtime checks with a unified validator that enforces cross-region/tier contracts and safe fallback model variants at policy ingestion time.

Background: The current routing ingestion performs patchy runtime guards which leads to edge-case failures (e.g., model fallback to a quantized variant without required KV-cache compatibility or region-exclusive model variants leaking into other regions). This ticket implements a compile-time (ingestion-time) validator that: 
- Verifies region->tier contracts (e.g., a tier in eu-west must only reference models tagged for eu-region unless explicit cross_region:true).
- Enforces tier capacity ratios and warns if suggested fallbacks could violate latency SLOs (heuristic check using model perf table).
- Validates allowed_fallbacks list: ensure fallback model variant is architecture-compatible (KV cache, context-length) and present in the model catalog for the target region.
- Provides lintable autofix suggestions for common misconfigurations and a non-blocking "soft-mode" for gradual rollout.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) New validator runs during policy create/update in the control plane and rejects invalid configs with actionable diagnostics.
2) Unit + integration tests cover regional constraints, tier-ratio warnings, and fallback compatibility matrix.
3) Migration tool that scans existing policies and emits a report + suggested fixes; non-destructive by default.
4) CI gate added for policy schema changes; security review completed.

Design highlights / tradeoffs: 
- We intentionally separate strict vs soft enforcement. Early adopter customers can opt into strict enforcement to prevent runtime surprises; for others we emit warnings and a grace period.
- We will embed a lightweight model-compatibility heuristic in the validator (quantization flag + min_context_len + kv_cache_compatible). This avoids expensive runtime probing but requires keeping the model catalog metadata accurate.
- To avoid creating a new DSL, we extend current policy schema with three optional fields: allowed_fallbacks (list), cross_region (bool), tier_capacity_ratio (decimal). These fields are additive to maintain backcompat.

Migration plan: 
1) Run offline scanner (scan-policies job) on all live policies; generate CSV with issues and suggested edits.
2) Outreach to customers with high-risk configs; open a remediation ticket for those we will automatically fix.
3) Enable soft-mode enforcement for two weeks, then flip to strict for new writes.
4) Rollback: revert validator to soft-mode + enable emergency bypass flag for control plane operator if false positives found.

Test plan: 
- Unit tests (validator logic matrix) covering 120+ permutations of region/tier/fallback combos.
- Integration tests in staging using policy fixtures and a small model-catalog snapshot.
- Canary on 5% of policy writes for 72 hours before wide rollout.

Monitoring / observability: 
- Add telemetry: policy_validation_result (pass/warn/fail), validation_latency_ms, catalog_mismatch_count.
- Dashboard: validation failure trends by project/region and top offending rules.

Rollout steps: 
- Merge feature branch behind feature flag: routing.validator.v2
- Deploy control-plane canary, enable soft-mode for canary orgs
- Run scan-policies job and publish remediation CSV to drive
- After two-week soft period, enable strict enforcement for all new writes
- Schedule follow-up (30d) to evaluate false-positive rate and customer support load.
